Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just be identified as the driver of the vehicle, if that's alright.
Q: That works. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was going through an intersection in Conroe, Texas, heading east on the main road. The light had been green for
me as I approached.
Q: What happened as you entered the intersection?
A: A car coming from the cross street on my right pushed through and hit the side of my vehicle, right behind the front
door. I had just started to move through when it happened.
Q: Did you have any time to react before the impact?
A: Not really. I saw the other car at the last second and tried to brake, but there wasn't enough room.
Q: Were you injured?
A: Yes. My neck snapped forward and then back, and my head hit the side window. I felt stiffness right away, and by
the next morning the pain had spread into my shoulders and upper back.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon and I've been seeing a physical therapist twice a week since
then. The doctor said I have soft tissue damage in my neck.
Q: Do you have any pre-existing neck or back problems?
A: No, nothing that had required treatment before this. I was working full time and driving daily without restriction.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm still having headaches and I've had to limit how long I can sit at my desk. I'd like the claim to reflect
that.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
</page>
